newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude firmer but wet market inactive.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude firmer but wet market inactive.

text.p: Brent crude cash values were slightly higher in line with firmer futures but the wet market was depressed with physical deals scarce and sellers resigned to lower levels for both Brent and alternative North Sea grades.
"There is no direction or incentive to do any business," a wet dealer said. "The market is not clear and there is a big gap between buyers and sellers."
December Brent was notionally assessed around screen levels of $23.80-$23.85 a barrel at midday. No outright deals were heard and spreads were virtually unchanged on late Wednesday's levels.
Brokers said Dec/Jan was talked around +42/+45 cents and Jan/Feb at +54/+57 cents.
A CFD trade for Nov 11-15 dates was heard done at Dec -20 cents, some five cents up from bids late on Wednesday.
The last cargo of Brent traded at Dec -35 cents for a Nov 12-14 loader but that was before Wednesday's clocking of a Nov 13-15 loader, which the holders were trying to defer to Thursday.
"Crude is a tad stronger this morning and we're not too sure why. I don't see any good demand and the arbitrage (to the U.S.) is not looking good," a trader for a major said.
"We might see some interest if Dated stays at these depressed levels," he added.
One trading house is showing a ULCC load of Brent in the U.S. Gulf at WTI +25 or as low as WTI +15 cents but finding no takers, U.S. traders said.

Analysts say the fall in weekly crude stocks as shown by the API on Tuesday could be explained by the fact that North Sea and Nigerian grades were not going into the U.S. Gulf. The London trader said refinery margins were looking better and might spur demand but an oversupply of North Sea grades was unlikely to see differentials repeat the lofty levels seen earlier in the month.
